persuade.situation: Your whole class thinks the exam is too soon. Convince the teacher to move it to next week.

persuade.team: Student council who wants to change the uniform rule
persuade.situation: The whole student council thinks the school uniform is old and boring. Convince the principal to let students wear casual clothes every Friday.

persuade.team: Students who think the homework is not fair
persuade.situation: Your whole class thinks this week's homework is too long and not fair. Convince the teacher to cancel it completely.

persuade.team: Students who all missed the deadline
persuade.situation: Many students missed the project deadline because the instructions were not clear. Convince the professor to give everyone one more week.

persuade.team: Students who want to do something creative
persuade.situation: The whole class wants to replace the final exam with a fun group project or show. Convince the teacher it is a great way to learn.

persuade.team: Students who want a game room at school
persuade.situation: A group of students wants to turn an empty room into a place to play games and relax. Convince the principal it will help students do better in class.

persuade.team: Students who want class outside today
persuade.situation: It is a beautiful sunny day and everyone wants to have class outside in the garden. Convince the teacher to leave the classroom just this one time.

persuade.team: Students who want better school food
persuade.situation: The whole student group thinks the school food is boring and not healthy. Convince the cafeteria manager to change the menu and make it better.

persuade.team: Students who want a longer lunch break
persuade.situation: Everyone feels the lunch break is too short. Convince the principal to make it 30 minutes longer every day.

persuade.team: Students who want a school trip
persuade.situation: The whole class wants to go on a school trip instead of normal classes for a week. Convince the principal it is a great way to learn outside the classroom.

persuade.team: Employees who want to work from home
persuade.situation: Your whole team wants to work from home every Friday. Convince the manager that the work will still get done and everyone will be happier.

persuade.team: Team members who want more money for projects
persuade.situation: Your team does not have enough money to do their work well. Convince the CEO to give the team twice as much money for the next three months.

persuade.team: Employees who want free lunch and a rest room
persuade.situation: The whole team wants free lunch every Friday and a quiet room to rest during the day. Convince the HR manager it will make the team work much better.

persuade.team: Employees who hate the early morning meeting
persuade.situation: Nobody likes the 8am Monday meeting. Convince the boss to move it to Wednesday at 11am instead.

persuade.team: Employees who want a "bring your pet" day
persuade.situation: The whole team wants to bring their pets to the office once a month. Convince the boss it will make everyone less stressed and more friendly with each other.

persuade.team: Employees who want a 4-day work week
persuade.situation: Everyone in the company wants to work only 4 days a week but get the same pay. Convince the CEO the company will do better and people will work harder.

persuade.team: Employees who want extra rest days
persuade.situation: Your team wants the company to give everyone two extra paid "rest days" per year. Convince the HR manager it is good for everyone.

persuade.team: Employees who want a fun room in the office
persuade.situation: A group of workers wants to build a game room and a relaxing area in the office. Convince the CEO it will help the team think more clearly and work better.

persuade.team: Employees who want family visit days
persuade.situation: The team wants to invite their families to the office on the last Friday of every month. Convince the HR manager it will make workers feel happier and more connected.

persuade.team: Employees who want a casual dress code
persuade.situation: Everyone is tired of wearing formal clothes to the office every day. Convince the manager to change the dress code to casual clothes from Monday to Friday.

persuade.team: Residents who want a community garden
persuade.situation: Your group wants to turn the empty land on Main Street into a garden and playground for everyone. Convince the mayor to say yes and help pay for it.

persuade.team: Tenants who want better living conditions
persuade.situation: All the people in the building want the landlord to fix the broken lift, add free WiFi, and allow pets. Convince the landlord to agree to all three.

persuade.team: Parents who want a no-phone rule at school
persuade.situation: A group of parents wants the school to not allow phones during school hours. Convince the principal to start this rule next month.

persuade.team: Young people who want a skate park
persuade.situation: A group of young people wants the city to build a free skate park and sports area. Convince the city council it will keep young people active and happy.

persuade.team: Residents who want longer library hours
persuade.situation: People in the area want the library to stay open until midnight. Convince the director this will help students and people who like to read at night.

persuade.team: Residents who want car-free Sundays
persuade.situation: Your group wants to close the main street to cars every Sunday so people can walk and ride bikes freely. Convince the mayor to try this idea.

persuade.team: Residents who want a street party
persuade.situation: Your group wants to hold a big free street party with food, music, and fun activities. Convince the city council to say yes and give a small amount of money.

persuade.team: Residents who want a park instead of a car park
persuade.situation: The city wants to build a big car park in your area. Convince the city planner to turn that space into a nice green park with trees and seats instead.

persuade.team: All the kids who want to go to a theme park
persuade.situation: All the children want to go to a theme park for the family holiday instead of visiting family. Convince your parents it will be much more fun and a memory they will never forget.

persuade.team: Grandchildren who want grandma to get a smartphone
persuade.situation: The whole family wants grandma to get a smartphone so everyone can video call her. Convince her it is easy to use and will help keep the family close.

persuade.team: Siblings who want a new games console
persuade.situation: All the brothers and sisters want a new games console. Convince your parents it helps with teamwork and everyone will set a time limit.

persuade.team: Kids who really want a family dog
persuade.situation: All the children want a dog. Convince dad that everyone will help look after it and the whole family will be happier.

persuade.team: Kids who want to stay up for New Year's Eve
persuade.situation: All the children want to stay up past midnight for New Year's Eve. Convince the parents this only happens once a year and everyone will be fine the next day.

persuade.team: Kids who want a surprise road trip
persuade.situation: The children want to skip school on Friday for a 3-day road trip with the family. Convince your parents it will be the best family memory ever.

persuade.team: Family members who want to go camping
persuade.situation: Everyone wants to go camping in the forest instead of the usual big formal dinner at a restaurant. Convince the grandparents that camping will be much more fun.

persuade.team: Kids who want a bigger TV
persuade.situation: Everyone at home wants to change the old small TV for a big new smart TV. Convince your parents it is a good thing to buy for the whole family.

persuade.team: Siblings who all want their own phone
persuade.situation: All the brothers and sisters feel they are the only kids without a phone. Convince your parents that phones are useful, safe, and easy to manage with some rules.

persuade.team: Kids who want to redecorate their rooms
persuade.situation: All the children want to give their rooms a new look with different colours and new things on the walls. Convince your parents to let everyone give their room a fresh new style.

persuade.judge: One friend who doesn't want to go
persuade.team: Friends who need everyone on the trip
persuade.situation: The whole group has planned a trip but one person keeps saying no. Convince them to come — you really need everyone there to make it the best trip ever.

persuade.team: Group members who want to go to the beach instead
persuade.situation: The group first planned to go to the mountains, but now almost everyone wants to go to the beach. Convince the person who planned it to change the place.

persuade.judge: One friend who wants to go home early
persuade.team: Friends who want to stay at the party
persuade.situation: It is only 9pm and one friend already wants everyone to go home. Convince them to stay at least two more hours — the fun is just starting.

persuade.judge: The one friend who always says no to karaoke
persuade.team: Friends who love karaoke
persuade.situation: Everyone wants to go to karaoke but one person says no every single time. Convince them that this time will be different — and they will really enjoy it.

persuade.judge: The laziest friend in the group
persuade.team: Friends who want to do a fitness challenge
persuade.situation: The whole group wants to do a 30-day fitness challenge together. Convince the laziest friend that it will be fun and not as hard as they think.

persuade.judge: The friend who is not sure about the food
persuade.team: The group who wants to try a very different restaurant
persuade.situation: Your group wants to eat at a restaurant that serves very unusual food. Convince the most careful eater in the group to give it a try — they might love it.

persuade.judge: The friend who organised the house party
persuade.team: Friends who want to go camping instead
persuade.situation: Your friend worked hard to plan a house party, but now everyone wants to go camping instead. Convince the organiser to change the plan.

persuade.judge: The shyest person in the group
persuade.team: Friends who want to start a band
persuade.situation: The group wants to start a band and play at the school show. Convince the shyest person to be the lead singer — the band really needs their voice.

persuade.judge: The friend who thinks it's too much work
persuade.team: Friends who want to plan a surprise party
persuade.situation: The group wants to plan a big surprise party for a close friend. Convince the one who thinks it is too much work that it will be easy, fun, and totally worth it.

persuade.judge: The friend who never wants to go out
persuade.team: Friends who want a picnic in the park
persuade.situation: The group wants to go to the park for a picnic on a sunny day, but one friend always wants to stay home. Convince them that fresh air and good food with friends is the best plan.

persuade.team: Friends who want to try a new hobby
persuade.situation: The whole group wants to try pottery or painting together. Convince the most resistant friend that it will be a fun and relaxing way to spend time together.

persuade.team: Friends who want to do a charity run
persuade.situation: The whole group wants to sign up for a charity run together. Convince the friend who hates running that it is for a good cause — and they do not need to run fast.

persuade.team: Players who want fewer training days
persuade.situation: The whole team thinks training six days a week is too much and people are getting hurt. Convince the coach to cut it down to four days and keep the team strong.

persuade.team: Players who think the call was wrong
persuade.situation: Your team thinks the referee made a bad call that could cost you the game. Convince the referee to change the decision before the final whistle.

persuade.team: Players who want to design their own team shirt
persuade.situation: The whole team is tired of the boring old team shirt. Convince the coach and the sponsor to let the players make their own new design for next season.

persuade.team: A group who had a very bad dinner experience
persuade.situation: Your whole group got cold food, waited over an hour, and had rude service. Convince the restaurant manager to give everyone a full refund.

persuade.team: Guests who had problems at check-in
persuade.situation: Your group booked three rooms but they were not ready when you arrived — two hours late with no sorry. Convince the hotel manager to give everyone a better room for free.

persuade.team: Passengers who missed their next flight
persuade.situation: Your whole group missed a flight because the airline's first flight was late. Convince the airline staff to put everyone on a new flight for free and give a food voucher.

persuade.team: A group who wants to see a special show
persuade.situation: The special show at the museum is fully booked for two months. Convince the museum staff to let your group in for a private visit after the museum closes.

persuade.team: A group of fans outside a sold-out event
persuade.situation: The event is sold out and your group is standing outside. Convince the event manager that letting your group in will only make the atmosphere even better.

persuade.team: A large group who wants a discount
persuade.situation: Your whole group wants to visit the theme park but the tickets are very expensive. Convince the manager to give the whole group a big discount for coming together.

persuade.team: Guests who want the pool to stay open late
persuade.situation: Your group wants to swim in the hotel pool at night, but it closes at 8pm. Convince the hotel manager to keep the pool open until 11pm just for your group tonight.

persuade.team: Tourists who want one more stop on the tour
persuade.situation: Your group loves the tour but wants to add one more interesting place before it ends. Convince the tour guide to take you there — even if it is a little extra time.

persuade.team: Kids who want to skip school for a gaming day
persuade.situation: Everyone wants to skip school on Friday to stay home and play video games all day together. Convince your parents that one day off will not hurt and it will be an amazing memory.

persuade.team: Students with a very creative excuse
persuade.situation: Nobody in the class did their homework. Convince the teacher that a strong wind came through the window and blew everyone's homework away before they could hand it in.

persuade.team: Employees who want to wear pyjamas on Fridays
persuade.situation: The whole team wants to wear their pyjamas to the office every Friday. Convince the boss that everyone will be more relaxed and do better work in comfortable clothes.

persuade.team: Grandchildren who want a spicy food challenge
persuade.situation: The whole family wants to do a very spicy food challenge together at dinner. Convince the grandparents to join in — it will be the funniest family moment ever.

persuade.team: Students who want a "bring your pet" day
persuade.situation: The whole school wants one special day where students can bring their pets to school. Convince the principal it will make everyone very happy and be a day no one forgets.

persuade.team: Students who want a snack break in the library
persuade.situation: Everyone studying in the library is hungry and tired. Convince the librarian to allow a short snack break in the middle of study time — just 10 quiet minutes.

persuade.team: Kids who want an all-night movie night
persuade.situation: Everyone wants to stay up all night watching films together. Convince your parents to join in and make it a big, fun family night that nobody will ever forget.

persuade.team: Players who want a water fight instead of training
persuade.situation: It is very hot and nobody wants to do normal training today. Convince the coach to let the whole team have a water fight instead — it is still a team activity!

persuade.team: A group who wants to use the neighbour's garden
persuade.situation: Your group wants to have a big BBQ party but needs more space. Convince your neighbour to let everyone use their garden for the afternoon.

persuade.team: A group with no money but lots of talent
persuade.situation: Your group has eaten a great meal but has no money to pay. Convince the restaurant owner to let everyone pay with a song and a short dance instead of money.

persuade.team: Students who want a pillow fight as a class activity
persuade.situation: The class wants to have a big pillow fight as a "team activity". Convince the teacher this is a real way to build friendship and have a lot of fun together.

persuade.team: Kids who want a snacks-only dinner
persuade.situation: Nobody wants real food tonight. Convince your parents to let everyone eat only snacks and sweet things for dinner — just this one time as a special treat.

persuade.team: Employees who want an afternoon off to play games
persuade.situation: It has been a very hard week and the whole team is tired. Convince the boss to cancel all work for one afternoon so everyone can relax and play board games together.

persuade.team: Students who want to teach the classes for one day
persuade.situation: The whole class wants to be the teachers for one day and teach their own lessons. Convince the principal this is a fun and creative way to learn.

persuade.team: Guests who want to build a fort in the lobby
persuade.situation: Your group wants to use the hotel sofas and blankets to build a giant fort in the lobby for the evening. Convince the hotel manager it will be harmless and very fun for everyone.

persuade.team: A group who wants a bubble contest in the park
persuade.situation: Your group wants to have a big bubble-blowing contest in the park. Convince the manager to let you use a small area — and maybe even join in.

persuade.team: Kids who want a pet goat
persuade.situation: Everyone in the family wants to get a pet goat for the garden. Convince your parents that a goat is a great pet, easy to look after, and will make the garden much more fun.

persuade.team: Students who want class in the swimming pool
persuade.situation: The whole class wants to move today's lesson to the school swimming pool. Convince the teacher it is still a proper class — just with more water.

persuade.team: Kids who want a matching funny costume day
persuade.situation: All the children want the whole family to put on matching funny costumes and spend the whole day out in town. Convince your parents it will be the most fun family day ever.

persuade.team: A group who wants to stay after closing time
persuade.situation: Your group is having such a great time at the café but it is closing time. Convince the owner to let everyone stay for a short singing competition before leaving.

persuade.team: Students who want a dance break in class
persuade.situation: The whole class is tired and wants to stop the lesson for a 5-minute group dance. Convince the teacher it will help everyone focus much better afterwards.

persuade.team: Kids who want breakfast food for dinner
persuade.situation: Nobody wants a normal dinner tonight. Convince your parents to let everyone eat pancakes, eggs, and toast for dinner instead — just for fun.

persuade.team: Employees who want to work from a café or park
persuade.situation: The whole team wants to work outside — at a café or in the park — for just one day. Convince the boss it will make everyone more creative and happy.

persuade.team: Grandchildren who want grandma to try video games
persuade.situation: The whole family wants grandma to try playing a simple video game for the first time. Convince her it is easy, very fun, and a great way to spend time together.

persuade.team: Students who want a silly hat day
persuade.situation: The whole school wants one day where everyone can wear their silliest or funniest hat to school. Convince the principal it will make everyone smile and bring the school together.

persuade.team: Kids who want to make a funny family video
persuade.situation: All the children want the whole family to make a short funny video together and post it online. Convince your parents it will be a fun memory and totally harmless.

persuade.team: Players who want music during training
persuade.situation: The whole team wants to play their favourite music out loud during every training session. Convince the coach it will make everyone more excited and work harder.

persuade.team: Students who want to choose the next topic
persuade.situation: The whole class wants to vote and choose what topic they study next. Convince the teacher that letting students choose will make everyone much more interested in learning.

persuade.team: Kids who want a picnic on the living room floor
persuade.situation: Everyone wants to eat dinner on a big blanket on the living room floor like a picnic instead of at the table. Convince your parents it will be a fun and different evening.

persuade.team: Employees who want a superhero costume day
persuade.situation: The whole team wants to wear superhero costumes to the office for one day. Convince the boss it will be a great way to laugh together and make the day more fun.

persuade.team: Students who want to read outside today
persuade.situation: The weather is beautiful and the whole group wants to take their books and read outside under the trees. Convince the librarian to let everyone go outside just for today.

persuade.team: Grandchildren who want grandparents on a roller coaster
persuade.situation: Your group wants your grandparents to try a roller coaster for the very first time. Convince them it is safe, quick, and they will love the feeling.

persuade.team: Students who want a movie day as a reward
persuade.situation: The class has been working very hard all week. Convince the teacher to have a movie day instead of a normal lesson as a special reward for everyone.

persuade.team: Kids who want to cook the whole family dinner
persuade.situation: All the children want to plan and cook dinner for the whole family tonight — all by themselves. Convince your parents to stay out of the kitchen and let the kids take over.

persuade.team: Members who want a dessert bar in the gym
persuade.situation: The whole group wants the gym to add a fun dance class and a small dessert bar after workouts. Convince the manager it will make people enjoy the gym much more.

persuade.team: A group who wants a silly sports day in the street
persuade.situation: Your group wants to set up a fun and silly sports day on the street — with egg-and-spoon races, sack races, and more. Convince your neighbour to close the street and join in.

persuade.team: Students who want a funny school mascot
persuade.situation: Students want to create a funny mascot costume that someone wears at school events. Convince the principal it will make the school more fun and everyone will love it.

persuade.team: Kids who want a family role-swap day
persuade.situation: All the children want the whole family to swap their daily jobs and roles for one day — kids act as parents, parents act as kids. Convince mom and dad to give it a try.

persuade.team: Students who want a nap time in class
persuade.situation: Everyone in class is very tired and wants a 15-minute nap break in the middle of the lesson. Convince the teacher that a short rest will help everyone learn better after.

scene.title: Coffee Shop Chaos
scene.situation: One customer can't decide what to order. The line is getting longer. Everyone has an opinion.

a.label: The Lost Customer
a.hint: You want 'something good' but have no idea what. You keep asking B and C for help.

b.label: The Sleepy Barista
b.hint: You just need A to pick something. Anything. Please. You've been here since 6am.

c.label: The Helpful Friend
c.hint: You have lots of drink ideas for A — but you change your mind every 10 seconds.

d.label: The Person Behind in Line
d.hint: You've waited too long. You shout suggestions at A and argue with C's ideas.

e.label: The Store Manager
e.hint: You're watching from behind the counter. This has never happened before. You're deciding whether to step in.

f.label: The Regular Customer
f.hint: You come here every single day. You've never seen anything like this. You have strong opinions and you will share them.

scene.title: The Party Escape
scene.situation: One person is trying to leave the party. Their friend refuses to let them go.

a.label: The One Who Wants to Leave
a.hint: You don't know anyone here. The music is too loud. You just want to go home.

b.label: The Excited Friend
b.hint: You brought A here. If A leaves, you'll feel bad. You NEED A to have fun.

c.label: The Friendly Stranger
c.hint: You want to be friends with A. You keep talking to A without noticing A wants to escape.

d.label: The Party Host
d.hint: Every time A moves toward the door, you appear with food, games, or a new activity.

e.label: The Uber Driver
e.hint: You're parked outside. You've sent A three messages already. You're about to cancel the ride.

f.label: The Person at the Door
f.hint: You're trying to get in. A keeps bumping into you on the way out. This is very confusing for you.

scene.title: The Worst Interview
scene.situation: A job interview is happening — and things keep going wrong for everyone in the room.

a.label: The Nervous Candidate
a.hint: You really need this job. But every answer you give sounds worse than the last.

b.label: The Distracted Interviewer
b.hint: You're supposed to ask A questions, but your phone keeps buzzing with urgent texts.

c.label: The Too-Happy HR Person
c.hint: You think everything A says is AMAZING — even when it's clearly not.

d.label: The Next Candidate
d.hint: You're waiting outside but you keep walking in at the worst possible moments.

e.label: The Receptionist
e.hint: You keep calling the room phone about completely unimportant things. You sound very urgent every time.

f.label: The IT Person
f.hint: You barge in to fix the projector right in the middle of A's most important answer. You take your time.

scene.title: Flight Delay Madness
scene.situation: The flight is delayed. Nobody knows why. The gate keeps changing. People are getting upset.

a.label: The Stressed Traveler
a.hint: You MUST be somewhere important. You keep asking B what is going on.

b.label: The Airport Staff
b.hint: You want to help A but you don't actually have any real answers right now.

c.label: The Confident Wrong Person
c.hint: You've been here before. You give A a lot of advice. Most of it is wrong.

d.label: The Phone Talker
d.hint: You're on a call, saying everything that happens OUT LOUD. Very loudly.

e.label: The Pilot
e.hint: You wander through the gate area in full uniform. You won't explain what's happening. You look very relaxed.

f.label: The Child Traveling Alone
f.hint: You ask A for help because A looks like they know what's going on. A does not know what's going on.

scene.title: Gym Day One
scene.situation: It's your first day at the gym. You have no idea what to do. Three people all want to help — sort of.

a.label: The Lost Beginner
a.hint: You don't know how anything works. You just press buttons and hope for the best.

b.label: The Gym Expert
b.hint: You've given A five tips already. A didn't ask for any of them. You have more.

c.label: The Competitive One
c.hint: You want to race A, out-lift A, or beat A at everything. Everything is a contest.

d.label: The Gym Staff
d.hint: Your job is to help A. But your phone is much more interesting right now.

e.label: The Machine Hogger
e.hint: You've been on the machine A needs for 45 minutes. You're not leaving anytime soon. You have one more set.

f.label: The Gym Influencer
f.hint: You're filming everything for content. You just filmed A's most embarrassing moment. You haven't decided whether to post it.

scene.title: Dinner Disaster
scene.situation: The host cooked for three hours. The food is… not great. Everyone is trying to react nicely.

a.label: The Proud Host
a.hint: You worked very hard. You are watching everyone's face very, very carefully.

b.label: The Honest Guest
b.hint: You can't fake a reaction. Your face always shows exactly what you think.

c.label: The Worried Friend
c.hint: You can see B's face. You jump in with nice words before A notices B's reaction.

d.label: The Over-Actor
d.hint: You're pretending to LOVE the food. Way too much. Nobody believes you.

e.label: The Allergic Guest
e.hint: You quietly realize you're allergic to the main ingredient. You haven't told anyone yet. You are making a decision.

f.label: The Delivery Driver
f.hint: Someone secretly ordered real food as backup. It just arrived. You ring the doorbell at the worst possible moment.

scene.title: Library War
scene.situation: Someone is very noisy in a quiet library. The librarian is coming. Someone is trying to help — but making things worse.

a.label: The Stressed Student
a.hint: You have an exam tomorrow. This noise is killing you. You need silence NOW.

b.label: The Noisy One
b.hint: You don't think you're loud. Every time C warns you, you get a little louder.

c.label: The Librarian
c.hint: You've told B to be quiet three times. You're very calm. This is your final warning.

d.label: The Helper
d.hint: You want to help A and C, but every idea you have makes B more upset.

e.label: The Sleeping Snorer
e.hint: You fell asleep at your desk. You are now snoring loudly. You have no idea this is happening.

f.label: The Library Security Guard
f.hint: C called you in as backup. You arrive. You have a very long list of library rules to read out loud.

scene.title: The Waiting Room
scene.situation: People are waiting at the doctor's office. Nobody knows how long the wait will be.

a.label: The Very Impatient One
a.hint: You've asked D 'how long?' several times already. You're going to ask again. Right now.

b.label: The Very Calm One
b.hint: You don't mind waiting at all. You have snacks and a book. You offer A a snack.

c.label: The Oversharer
c.hint: You want to tell everyone why you're here. In detail. You want everyone's opinion.

d.label: The Receptionist
d.hint: You don't know when anyone will be called. A won't stop asking. C won't stop talking.

e.label: The One Just Called In
e.hint: You arrived after everyone else. Somehow you get called first. You can feel A's eyes on your back.

f.label: The Doctor
f.hint: You poke your head out for one second, smile at everyone, then disappear back inside. No explanation at all.

scene.title: One Item Left
scene.situation: There is ONE item left on the shelf. Two people grabbed it at the same time. Neither will let go.

a.label: The First Grabber
a.hint: You saw it first. Your hand touched it first. It's yours. End of story.

b.label: The Other Grabber
b.hint: You ALSO saw it first. Your hand ALSO touched it first. It's yours. End of story.

c.label: The Random Helper
c.hint: You saw the whole thing. You're trying to find a fair answer. Your ideas are not great.

d.label: The Store Worker
d.hint: You have to solve this. You really don't want to. You just want to go back to work.

e.label: The Emotional Gift Buyer
e.hint: It's a birthday gift for your child. You have a very moving reason for needing it. You begin to explain. At length.

f.label: The Store Manager
f.hint: You announce there's one more in the back — but you'll only bring it out for the person with the best reason.

scene.title: Lost on a Road Trip
scene.situation: You're in a car together. You're lost. The GPS is broken. Everyone has a different plan.

a.label: The Stubborn Driver
a.hint: You won't stop. You won't ask for help. You have a 'feeling' about the right way.

b.label: The Bad Navigator
b.hint: You're reading the map. You've given three wrong turns. You won't say sorry.

c.label: The Hungry Passenger
c.hint: You stopped caring about directions. You just need food. Any food. Please.

d.label: The Happy Passenger
d.hint: Everything is great! This is an adventure! You don't understand why everyone is upset.

e.label: The Traffic Police Officer
e.hint: You pull the car over. A drove the wrong way down a one-way street. You have many questions. And a notepad.

f.label: The Hitchhiker
f.hint: A picked you up a few miles back. You claim to know the way perfectly. Your confidence is very high.

scene.title: Movie Night Fight
scene.situation: A group of friends want to watch a movie together. Nobody can agree on what to pick.

a.label: The Horror Fan
a.hint: Every good movie is scary. If it's not scary, why are you watching it?

b.label: The Romance Fan
b.hint: You want something happy. No blood. No monsters. Something that makes you cry in a good way.

c.label: The Smart Movie Person
c.hint: You want a documentary or a foreign film. Something with meaning.

d.label: The "Fine With Anything" Person
d.hint: You say you're okay with anything. But you say 'no' to every single suggestion.

e.label: The One Who Falls Asleep
e.hint: No matter what movie is picked, you fall asleep within 10 minutes. You still have very strong opinions about what to watch.

f.label: The Uninvited Guest
f.hint: You just showed up. Nobody invited you. You have one specific movie recommendation and you will not leave until they agree.

scene.title: Hotel Mix-Up
scene.situation: You arrive at the hotel. Your room isn't ready. Something went wrong with the booking.

a.label: The Very Tired Guest
a.hint: You've been traveling all day. You need a bed NOW. Your eyes are closing.

b.label: The Calm Complainer
b.hint: You are very polite and very serious. You will not leave without a solution and a discount.

c.label: The Stranger in Line
c.hint: You're also checking in. You keep giving B advice on how to complain better. It makes things worse.

d.label: The Front Desk Person
d.hint: You're sorry about everything. The rules say you can't do more. B will not accept this.

e.label: The Guest Already in A's Room
e.hint: You have a key that also works. You've already unpacked. You're very confused about what's happening downstairs.

f.label: The Hotel Manager
f.hint: You have the power to fix everything. But you're on a personal call and keep waving everyone away.

scene.title: Midnight Convenience Store
scene.situation: It's 2am. One person is buying very strange things. The cashier has a lot of questions.

a.label: The Midnight Shopper
a.hint: The things in your basket look weird, but you have a perfectly good reason for each one. You explain them all to B.

b.label: The Sleepy Cashier
b.hint: You're supposed to scan things, not ask questions. But you have SO many questions about A's basket.

c.label: The Other Customer
c.hint: You came for one thing. Now you're deep in A's shopping choices. You have strong opinions.

d.label: The Store Manager
d.hint: You keep calling B on the store phone to check on something. B keeps ignoring you to talk to A and C.

e.label: The Night Delivery Person
e.hint: You arrive at 2am with a massive restock. You block the entire aisle. You need B's signature. Right now. It's urgent.

f.label: The Regular Night Customer
f.hint: You come here every night at this hour. You've seen everything. You offer A very strange and specific life advice.

scene.title: Group Project Disaster
scene.situation: One person did all the work. The presentation is in 10 minutes. The others just arrived.

a.label: The One Who Did Everything
a.hint: You're exhausted and furious. You have 10 minutes to teach B, C, and D everything about the project.

b.label: The Late Arrival
b.hint: You're very sorry. You want to help. But you have no idea what this project is even about.

c.label: The Confident One
c.hint: You haven't read a single page, but you're ready to present. You have a great gut feeling about it.

d.label: The Nervous One
d.hint: You read everything but you're too scared to speak. You keep whispering facts to A very quietly.

e.label: The Professor
e.hint: You arrive 10 minutes early to check on everyone. You can tell something is very wrong. You start asking questions.

f.label: The Other Group
f.hint: You're practicing right next to them — loudly and very confidently. This makes D significantly more nervous.

scene.title: The Ruined Surprise Party
scene.situation: Someone planned a surprise party. The birthday person already knows. Nobody knows that they know.

a.label: The Birthday Person
a.hint: You found out about the party last week. You're pretending to be surprised. It's very, very hard.

b.label: The Party Planner
b.hint: You worked so hard on this. You need A's reaction to be perfect. You keep watching A's face.

c.label: The One Who Told A
c.hint: You're the one who accidentally told A about the party. You're hoping nobody finds out it was you.

d.label: The Suspicious Guest
d.hint: You can tell A already knows. You keep giving C long, slow, suspicious looks.

e.label: The Oblivious One
e.hint: You have no idea A already knows. You keep dropping huge hints right in front of A. You think you're being extremely subtle.

f.label: The Hired Photographer
f.hint: You were paid to capture A's genuine surprise reaction. You follow A everywhere with a camera. The pressure is building.

scene.title: Wrong Yoga Class
scene.situation: Someone walked into the wrong yoga class. It's not for beginners. The class has already started.

a.label: The Lost Newcomer
a.hint: You thought this was 'gentle yoga for beginners.' You were very wrong. You can't do any of this.

b.label: The Serious Yogi
b.hint: You've practiced for 10 years. You are very upset about the energy in the room right now.

c.label: The Helpful Neighbor
c.hint: You're next to A and want to help. Your whispered instructions are making A more confused.

d.label: The Yoga Teacher
d.hint: You can see A is struggling badly. You keep giving A 'gentle encouragement' in a very calm, slow voice.

e.label: The Other Lost Person
e.hint: You also walked into the wrong class, five minutes after A. You are somehow much more relaxed about it than A.

f.label: The Studio Receptionist
f.hint: You come in to confirm whether A is supposed to be in this class. You do this in front of everyone, very loudly.

scene.title: Dog Park Chaos
scene.situation: One dog is causing trouble at the dog park. The owners all have very different reactions.

a.label: The Embarrassed Owner
a.hint: Your dog is causing all the problems. You can't stop saying sorry to everyone.

b.label: The Angry Dog Owner
b.hint: Your dog is the victim here. You want an apology from A. A full apology. Preferably in writing.

c.label: The Dog Whisperer
c.hint: You believe you can fix this by talking to the dogs. You think it's working. It's not working.

d.label: The Person Without a Dog
d.hint: You just came to sit on a bench and relax. Somehow you are now the most involved person here.

e.label: The Dog Park Ranger
e.hint: You have a rulebook. It is very long. You are going to read the relevant sections. Starting now.

f.label: The Third Dog Owner
f.hint: Your dog just joined the chaos. You pretend not to notice. You whistle casually and look at the sky.

scene.title: After the Karaoke Song
scene.situation: Someone just finished singing a very bad song. They think it was great. Everyone is trying to respond.

a.label: The Happy Singer
a.hint: You just finished. You thought it was great. You're waiting for everyone's honest feedback.

b.label: The Supportive Friend
b.hint: You're trying so hard to say something nice. You are running out of things to say.

c.label: The Honest Music Lover
c.hint: You care deeply about music. You're trying not to say what you really think. You're failing.

d.label: The MC
d.hint: You need to keep the energy going after that performance. It is much harder than you expected.

e.label: The Next Singer
e.hint: You signed up to go right after A. You've been waiting a long time. A still won't leave the stage or let go of the mic.

f.label: The Karaoke Bar Owner
f.hint: You came over to check that the sound equipment is still in working order. Your face says a lot.

scene.title: The Pizza Order
scene.situation: The group needs to order one pizza. Nobody can agree. The delivery person is waiting on the phone.

a.label: The Classic Person
a.hint: Plain cheese. No toppings. Perfect pizza. Simple. Why is everyone making this so hard?

b.label: The Topping Maximalist
b.hint: You want everything on it. Everything. The more toppings, the better. This is non-negotiable.

c.label: The Dietary Restriction Person
c.hint: You have a list of things you can't eat. It's a long list. You're reading it now. Slowly.

d.label: The Delivery Person (on phone)
d.hint: You've been listening to this argument for 5 minutes. You need a decision. RIGHT NOW.

e.label: The Secret Solo Orderer
e.hint: You quietly ordered your own personal pizza 10 minutes ago. It just arrived. You are eating it in the corner. Watching everyone.

f.label: The Wrong Pizza Driver
f.hint: You arrive with a completely different pizza from a previous order. You suggest everyone just take it. It's here. It's hot.

scene.title: One Bathroom, No Time
scene.situation: Roommates share one bathroom. Everyone has to be somewhere by 8am. It's 7:45.

a.label: The Running Late One
a.hint: You must leave in 10 minutes. You are not ready at all. You are knocking very loudly.

b.label: The One Inside
b.hint: You've been in the bathroom for 40 minutes. You're still not done. You're singing.

c.label: The Calm One
c.hint: You woke up early. You already have coffee. You're watching everything fall apart with great interest.

d.label: The One Still in Bed
d.hint: Everyone keeps knocking on your door to wake you up. You have very good reasons for staying in bed.

e.label: The Maintenance Worker
e.hint: You just showed up to fix the hot water. You need bathroom access. Right now. It is technically an emergency.

f.label: The Overnight Guest
f.hint: You stayed over last night. You also quietly need to use the bathroom. You don't know how to bring this up.

scene.title: Moving Day
scene.situation: Moving into a new place. The big sofa does not fit through the door. Everyone has a plan.

a.label: The Owner
a.hint: This is your sofa. You have opinions on how to move it. Your opinions change every two minutes.

b.label: The Mover
b.hint: You're getting paid to move things. You didn't know it would be this complicated. You're sweating.

c.label: The Friend Who Came to Help
c.hint: You said you'd help. You didn't know 'help' meant carrying heavy things. Your back hurts.

d.label: The New Neighbor
d.hint: You came to say hello. Now you're giving directions on how to angle the sofa through the door.

e.label: The Building Manager
e.hint: You arrive to announce the elevator can only be used until noon. It is currently 11:58am. You seem very calm about this.

f.label: The Previous Tenant
f.hint: You come back for something you left behind. You squeeze past the sofa situation. You make everything more complicated.

scene.title: Game Night Disaster
scene.situation: Board game night. One person is winning by a lot. One person has no idea what they're doing.

a.label: The Competitive Player
a.hint: You're here to win. You've been winning. You have no patience for beginners who slow things down.

b.label: The New Player
b.hint: This is your first time. You're losing badly. You think A is being mean on purpose.

c.label: The Rule Explainer
c.hint: You know every single rule and you need everyone to know that you know every single rule.

d.label: The Snack Person
d.hint: You came for the food and the company. You have zero interest in the game. You keep asking when it ends.

e.label: The House Rules Person
e.hint: You insist on your own special house rules. You claim they're the real official ones. Nobody agrees with you.

f.label: The Partner Who Wants to Leave
f.hint: You came with one of the players. You're completely done. You keep tapping their shoulder every few minutes.

scene.title: The Last Seat on the Bus
scene.situation: One seat left on a very crowded bus. Several people want it. The bus driver is watching.

a.label: The Exhausted Worker
a.hint: You've been standing for two hours. Your legs are giving up. You need this seat more than anyone.

b.label: The Person With Bags
b.hint: You have six bags and nowhere to put them. You need this seat for the bags. It makes sense to you.

c.label: The Too-Polite One
c.hint: You want the seat, but you keep offering it to A and B. You need to stop doing this. Please just sit down.

d.label: The Bus Driver
d.hint: You've been watching this in your mirror. You have one rule: sit down or stand up. Just decide. Please.

e.label: The Silent Charger
e.hint: You say nothing. You walk straight to the seat with total confidence. Nobody knows where you came from.

f.label: The Elderly Person Who Just Boarded
f.hint: You just got on the bus. Everyone is now looking at the seat, then at you, then back at the seat.

scene.title: The Sick Roommate
scene.situation: One roommate is sick at home. The others all react in very different ways.

a.label: The Sick One
a.hint: You feel terrible. You need soup and silence. Everyone is being very strange and you want them to stop.

b.label: The Worried Caretaker
b.hint: You looked up A's symptoms online. You have bad news. You're not a doctor but you have a diagnosis.

c.label: The Germaphobe
c.hint: You cannot be in the same room as A. You've been spraying disinfectant on everything, including B.

d.label: The Unbothered One
d.hint: You feel completely fine. You finished A's leftover soup. You don't understand why C is being so dramatic.

e.label: The Soup Delivery Person
e.hint: B ordered soup for A online. It just arrived. D has already eaten some of it. Nobody has told A yet.

f.label: The Doctor on Video Call
f.hint: B made a video appointment without telling A. The doctor joins the call. They have a lot of questions and some concerning follow-ups.

scene.title: Theme Park Queue
scene.situation: A 2-hour line for a ride. People are bored. Someone just jumped the queue near the front.

a.label: The Excited One
a.hint: You've wanted to go on this ride your whole life. The 2-hour wait is completely worth it. You're very happy.

b.label: The Bored One
b.hint: You had no idea the line was this long. You want to leave. A keeps talking you out of it.

c.label: The Queue Entertainer
c.hint: You've decided to keep everyone happy with games and jokes. You do this for 2 hours. Nobody asked you to.

d.label: The Queue Jumper
d.hint: You just walked to the front of the line. You have a 'very good reason.' A and B have strong feelings about this.

e.label: The Theme Park Employee
e.hint: You walk to the front and announce the ride has temporarily stopped. You don't know when it will restart. Sorry.

f.label: The Accidental Bumper
f.hint: You keep accidentally bumping into D while shuffling forward. Everyone thinks you're also jumping the queue. You're not.

scene.title: Escape Room: 5 Minutes Left
scene.situation: Your group is stuck in an escape room. 5 minutes left. You still haven't solved the last puzzle.

a.label: The Leader
a.hint: You've solved three clues already. You're in charge. Nobody is listening to you. You're losing your mind.

b.label: The Panicker
b.hint: You can't think. You keep picking things up and putting them back in the wrong place. Sorry.

c.label: The One Who's Been Here Before
c.hint: You did this room last year. You remember the answer but you don't want to ruin it for everyone.

d.label: The Phone Cheater
d.hint: The rules said no phones. You're on your phone. You found the answer online. Should you tell everyone?

e.label: The Game Master (on intercom)
e.hint: You deliver a cryptic hint every 60 seconds. The hints make no sense. Your voice is very calm. This somehow makes it worse.

f.label: The Staff Member
f.hint: You walk in to reset a prop. You accidentally make eye contact with the answer to the final puzzle. Very awkward.

scene.title: Beach Day Gone Wrong
scene.situation: A relaxing beach day. Nothing is relaxing.

a.label: The Over-Prepared One
a.hint: You brought sunscreen, chairs, umbrellas, food, a first-aid kit, and three towels. It's a lot.

b.label: The Under-Prepared One
b.hint: You brought nothing. You're already sunburned. You keep asking A for things. A has everything.

c.label: The Sandcastle Builder
c.hint: You're building a very serious sandcastle. You need space. You need silence. Don't talk to you right now.

d.label: The Wave Runner
d.hint: You keep running into the waves and splashing everyone. You think this is the best day ever.

e.label: The Beach Vendor
e.hint: You keep trying to sell A even more things. A is already carrying too much. You have a very good deal on hats.

f.label: The Lifeguard
f.hint: You are watching D from your chair very carefully. You are slowly standing up. You have a whistle. You are considering using it.

scene.title: Lost Tourist
scene.situation: A tourist is completely lost. They need help. Several people are trying to help — in very different ways.

a.label: The Lost Tourist
a.hint: You need to get to the train station. Your map is upside down. Your language skills are limited.

b.label: The Helpful Local
b.hint: You want to help A so much. But A's map is wrong and you both point in different directions.

c.label: The Other Tourist
c.hint: You're also lost, but you pretend you know where everything is. You're leading everyone the wrong way.

d.label: The Street Food Seller
d.hint: You keep offering everyone food instead of directions. But everyone is slowly getting interested in the food.

e.label: The Tour Guide
e.hint: You spot A and immediately try to recruit them into your paid tour group. It starts in 5 minutes. You are very persuasive.

f.label: The Local Police Officer
f.hint: You notice the growing confused crowd and come to investigate. You also don't speak A's language.

scene.title: The Unhealthy Order
scene.situation: At a restaurant. One person ordered something very unhealthy. The others have opinions.

a.label: The Happy Indulger
a.hint: You ordered the biggest thing on the menu. You're very happy. You will not explain or apologize.

b.label: The Healthy Eater
b.hint: You've eaten clean for three months. A's order is everything you've given up. You have a lot of feelings.

c.label: The Nutritionist Friend
c.hint: You didn't want to say anything. But now you can't stop. You're listing facts at A. A doesn't care.

d.label: The Server
d.hint: You just want to take everyone's order and go. This table has been talking for 15 minutes. Please.

e.label: The Eavesdropper at the Next Table
e.hint: You can hear everything. You loudly agree with every point C makes. You were not invited into this conversation.

f.label: The Restaurant Owner
f.hint: You come over to personally recommend even more indulgent dishes to A. You are immediately A's new best friend.

scene.title: One Umbrella, No Cover
scene.situation: It's suddenly raining very hard. One person has an umbrella. The others do not.

a.label: The Umbrella Owner
a.hint: It's YOUR umbrella. You're deciding who gets to share it. This is a lot of pressure.

b.label: The One Getting Wet
b.hint: You're standing in the rain right now. You're looking at A. You're very, very wet.

c.label: The Negotiator
c.hint: You're trying to find a fair system for sharing the umbrella. You have a full proposal ready.

d.label: The One Who Doesn't Mind Rain
d.hint: You think everyone is overreacting. You like rain. You keep saying so. Nobody cares.

e.label: The Umbrella Vendor
e.hint: You appear from nowhere selling umbrellas. The price is very high. You explain it's a fair price given the weather.

f.label: The Stranger With an Umbrella
f.hint: You also have an umbrella but you're not sharing — you have plans for it. You walk past. You feel everyone's eyes on you.

scene.title: Stuck in the Elevator
scene.situation: The elevator stopped between floors. Nobody knows how long it will take. The emergency button is making a strange sound.

a.label: The Claustrophobic One
a.hint: You're fine. You're completely fine. You are NOT fine. Please press the button again.

b.label: The Meditation Guide
b.hint: You suggest everyone breathe slowly. You begin leading a guided meditation. Nobody asked. You continue.

c.label: The One Late for Something
c.hint: You have a meeting in eight minutes. You keep saying this. The number keeps going down.

d.label: The Over-Preparer
d.hint: You somehow have snacks, a flashlight, and a deck of cards. You were ready for exactly this.

e.label: The Repair Person
e.hint: You're outside the door. You keep saying 'almost there.' You've said it four times. You say it again.

f.label: The Person Taking the Stairs
f.hint: You heard them, passed the door, and kept walking. You come back five minutes later with coffee. Just for yourself.

scene.title: First Day at the Office
scene.situation: Someone is starting their first day. Nobody told them where to sit, what to do, or where the bathroom is.

a.label: The New Employee
a.hint: You have no idea where anything is. You keep smiling and nodding like you do.

b.label: The Too-Helpful Colleague
b.hint: You won't leave A alone. You have explained the coffee machine three times. You're about to explain it again.

c.label: The Too-Busy Colleague
c.hint: You can't help right now. Maybe later. Definitely not now. You say this while walking very fast.

d.label: The Office Gossip
d.hint: You pull A aside to warn them about everyone in the office. You've known A for eleven minutes.

e.label: The IT Person
e.hint: A's computer still isn't set up. You're 'almost done.' You said this two hours ago. You say it again.

f.label: The CEO
f.hint: You think A is the new intern. You give A a coffee order. A is not the intern. A accepts the task anyway.

scene.title: Power Outage
scene.situation: The power just went out. Nobody knows why. It's dark, nobody can find the candles, and everyone has a different theory.

a.label: The Conspiracy Theorist
a.hint: This was not an accident. You have a list of suspects. You are sharing the list right now.

b.label: The One With 3% Battery
b.hint: You're using your phone as a flashlight. You are watching the number. 2%. 1%.

c.label: The Survival Expert
c.hint: You immediately start rationing food and water. You explain that help could be weeks away. You live in a city.

d.label: The One Who Just Wanted to Sleep
d.hint: This is perfect. You have no complaints. You were going to bed anyway. Goodnight.

e.label: The Neighbor With Power
e.hint: You're on a different circuit. Your lights are on. You come to check on everyone. You are very cheerful about this.

f.label: The Power Company Hotline
f.hint: C has been on hold for 40 minutes. You finally answer. You put them on hold again. You apologize very warmly.

scene.title: The Wedding Speech
scene.situation: It's time for the speech. The person giving it is not ready. Nobody is stopping this.

a.label: The Unprepared Speech Giver
a.hint: You have three pages of notes. None of them feel right. You're still editing as you walk to the microphone.

b.label: The Uninvited Speech Giver
b.hint: Nobody asked you to speak. You prepared one anyway. It is very long. You are already standing up.

c.label: The One Already Crying
c.hint: A hasn't said a word yet. You're already crying. You keep saying you're okay. You are not okay.

d.label: The Table Critic
d.hint: You have been to fourteen weddings. You are taking mental notes. The bar has been set. This is not clearing it.

e.label: The MC
e.hint: You were meant to introduce A in thirty seconds. Your introduction is now longer than A's speech. You keep going.

f.label: The Catering Staff
f.hint: You need to clear the tables. You were told to start right now. Speech or no speech, you begin collecting plates.

scene.title: Dentist's Waiting Room
scene.situation: Everyone is waiting to see the dentist. The room is very quiet. It doesn't stay quiet for long.

a.label: The Terrified Patient
a.hint: You haven't been in six years. Today you remember exactly why. You're reconsidering everything.

b.label: The Regular Patient
b.hint: You come every six months. No fear at all. You give A advice on staying calm. A did not ask for advice.

c.label: The It's-Just-a-Check-Up Patient
c.hint: Nothing is wrong with you. You feel guilty sitting next to A. You keep explaining that yours is very minor.

d.label: The Seven-Year-Old
d.hint: You are seven. You are not scared at all. You tell A there is nothing to be scared of. A is 34.

e.label: The Dental Nurse
e.hint: You call A's name. You are extremely cheerful. This is somehow making everything worse for A.

f.label: The Previous Patient
f.hint: You walk out holding your jaw. You make direct eye contact with A. You say nothing at all. You leave.

scene.title: Airport Security
scene.situation: The security line is long. Something has gone wrong at the scanner. Everyone is waiting.

a.label: The One Who Forgot the Liquids
a.hint: You remembered everything except the water bottle. You are now unpacking your entire bag onto the belt.

b.label: The One Behind A
b.hint: Your flight boards in eighteen minutes. You are watching A unpack. You are looking at your watch again.

c.label: The Over-Preparer
c.hint: Shoes off, belt off, watch off, laptop out, jacket folded before anyone asked. You are ready and you want credit for it.

d.label: The One Who Set Off the Alarm
d.hint: You walked through. The alarm went off. You don't know why. They don't know why. Everyone is waiting.

e.label: The Security Officer
e.hint: You are thorough. The line is very long. You are not going faster. You have a job to do and you are doing it.

f.label: The One Pulled Aside
f.hint: It's D. You're taken to a separate area. There is one very specific item in your bag. You forgot about it completely.

scene.title: The Camping Trip
scene.situation: The group arrived at the campsite. The tent isn't up. It's getting dark. Everyone is hungry and someone is trying to start a fire.

a.label: The "Experienced" Camper
a.hint: You've done this before. Twice. You're in charge. You keep reminding everyone you've done this before.

b.label: The One Who Packed Wrong
b.hint: You brought a suitcase. And a hair dryer. And nothing waterproof. You thought there would be a cabin.

c.label: The One Scared of the Outdoors
c.hint: There are sounds coming from the trees. The sounds are getting closer. You would like to leave. Right now.

d.label: The Marshmallow Person
d.hint: You don't care about the tent, the argument, or the sounds. You are here for the marshmallows. Only the marshmallows.

e.label: The Park Ranger
e.hint: You arrive with a list of regulations. The fire is in the wrong spot. The tent is too close to the trail. You have a notepad.

f.label: The Wildlife
f.hint: Something got into the food bag. A said to hang it from a tree. A did not hang it from a tree. The food is gone now.

scene.title: The Cooking Disaster
scene.situation: Someone offered to cook dinner for the whole group. An hour later, it is not going well.

a.label: The Cook Who Overcommitted
a.hint: You said thirty minutes. It has been ninety. The kitchen looks different now. You keep saying 'almost ready.'

b.label: The Kitchen Critic
b.hint: You've been watching since the start. You've counted eight mistakes. You've kept quiet. You are no longer keeping quiet.

c.label: The One Who Keeps Offering Help
c.hint: A said no help needed. You offered again after the smoke alarm. You are offering again right now.

d.label: The Very Hungry Guest
d.hint: You were told dinner at seven. It is now nine-thirty. You've eaten all the snacks. You're looking at the uncooked vegetables.

e.label: The Delivery Driver
e.hint: Someone secretly ordered a backup pizza. You've arrived with it. You ring the bell. A opens the door. A sees the box.

f.label: The Neighbor
f.hint: Your smoke alarm went off because of what's happening next door. You came to check. You see the pizza. You are staying for dinner.

scene.title: The Concert Queue
scene.situation: The doors open in two hours. The line is long. Someone just walked straight to the front.

a.label: The Line Guardian
a.hint: You have been here since six in the morning. These are your spots. You have a system. The system is being violated.

b.label: The Line Cutter
b.hint: You don't see a line as a rule. You see it as a suggestion. You went to the front. You don't understand the problem.

c.label: The One Who Left and Came Back
c.hint: You left to get food. You're back. You believe your spot is still yours. The situation around your spot is complicated.

d.label: The Very Relaxed Latecomer
d.hint: You arrived two minutes ago. You have a chair and a book. You don't know why anyone is stressed. You're having a wonderful time.

e.label: The Venue Staff
e.hint: You come out to announce there are fewer spots than expected. You say this very calmly. The line does not respond calmly.

f.label: The Ticket Scalper
f.hint: You have two extra tickets. You're walking the line slowly. You mention the price. Several people have strong feelings about the price.

scene.title: Wrong Rideshare
scene.situation: The driver picked up the wrong passenger. Both of them are fifteen minutes into the ride before anyone notices.

a.label: The Driver
a.hint: You picked up the wrong person. You realized five minutes ago. You are still driving. You are figuring out how to say this.

b.label: The Wrong Passenger
b.hint: You got in. The car matched. The name was close enough. You've been chatting happily with A for fifteen minutes.

c.label: The Right Passenger
c.hint: You're still outside. The app says your driver is arriving. Your driver has been 'arriving' for twenty-five minutes.

d.label: The Pool Passenger
d.hint: You were already in the car when A picked up B. You knew immediately something was wrong. You said nothing. You watched.

e.label: The Parking Officer
e.hint: A has been double-parked. You've been watching. You walk over with your ticket book. A is mid-conversation. You wait. Then you write.

f.label: The App Support Bot
f.hint: C called support. You are a very helpful automated system. You ask C to rate their recent trip. C has not taken their trip yet.
